subject: Ciências
description_pt: Discutir o papel do avanço tecnológico na aplicação das radiações na medicina diagnóstica (raio X, ultrassom, ressonância nuclear magnética) e no tratamento de doenças (radioterapia, cirurgia ótica a laser, infravermelho, ultravioleta etc.).

components.description_pt: Identificar tecnologias médicas diagnósticas que utilizam diferentes formas de radiação, como raios-X e ressonância magnética
components.description_en: Identify diagnostic medical technologies that use different forms of radiation, such as X-rays and MRI
components.cc_component_description: Explain how wave interactions with matter enable technologies such as medical imaging or communications

components.description_pt: Descrever como tipos específicos de radiação são aplicados no diagnóstico e tratamento de doenças
components.description_en: Describe how specific types of radiation are applied in medical diagnosis and disease treatment

components.description_pt: Discutir o papel do avanço tecnológico na expansão do uso médico da radiação
components.description_en: Discuss the role of technological advancement in expanding the medical use of radiation
components.cc_component_description: Explain the role of energy release or absorption in nuclear fusion, fission, and radioactive decay

components.description_pt: Avaliar os benefícios e riscos do uso de tecnologias baseadas em radiação na medicina
components.description_en: Evaluate the benefits and risks of using radiation-based technologies in medicine
components.cc_component_description: Compare the costs and benefits of different forms of energy production using evidence

cc_matches.description: Multiple technologies based on the understanding of waves and their interactions with matter are part of everyday experiences in the modern world (e.g., medical imaging, communications, scanners) and in scientific research. They are essential tools for producing, transmitting, and capturing signals and for storing and interpreting the information contained in them.

Nuclear processes, including fusion, fission, and radioactive decays of unstable nuclei, involve release or absorption of energy. The total number of neutrons plus protons does not change in any nuclear process.

All forms of energy production and other resource extraction have associated economic, social, environmental, and geopolitical costs and risks as well as benefits. New technologies and social regulations can change the balance of these factors.
